questions.question: What is the main variance-reduction idea behind bagging?
options: Fit models on bootstrap samples and average their predictions
Fit one model repeatedly on the same residual
Use only the single deepest tree
Replace all labels with their class frequencies
questions.explanation: Bootstrap samples create several related but different estimators; averaging their errors can cancel sampling variation.

questions.question: How does AdaBoost update its focus after a weak learner makes errors?
options: It deletes every correctly classified example
It increases the weights of misclassified examples
It shuffles the feature names but leaves example weights fixed
It fits only on the final test set
questions.explanation: AdaBoost gives more influence to examples the current learner gets wrong, so later learners concentrate on them.

questions.question: What target does a standard gradient-boosting stage fit after the current model?
options: A fresh random label for every row
The feature with the highest variance
The residual or negative loss gradient
The bootstrap index of the previous tree
questions.explanation: Each new learner approximates the direction that reduces the loss, commonly represented by residuals for squared-error regression.

questions.question: What source of diversity does BaggingClassifier add before it averages tree predictions?
options: It guarantees that every bootstrap row is unique
It fits one tree on the complete dataset and copies it
It uses validation labels to choose each tree
It fits each tree on a seeded bootstrap resample of the training rows
questions.explanation: BaggingClassifier samples training rows with replacement for each tree, so the fitted trees see different row multisets before their signed predictions are averaged.

questions.question: What is the role of the meta-learner in stacking?
options: It learns how to combine predictions from several base models
It replaces all base models with a nearest-neighbor lookup
It creates labels without observing the training target
It selects the first feature alphabetically
questions.explanation: Stacking feeds base-model predictions to a second model. Out-of-fold predictions are used for training that second model to limit leakage.

questions.question: Why can a majority vote improve as independent weak learners are added?
options: Each learner becomes perfect after the first vote
Their uncorrelated mistakes are less likely to occur in the same vote
The ensemble discards every minority class
Voting changes the features into bootstrap samples
questions.explanation: When errors are not perfectly correlated, the majority is increasingly likely to be correct as more learners vote.
